label: PF Backlog 576
title: Eventing SSOT: ADR + design (Go-first bus, Python thin client, no-duplication, migration)
body:
## Problem / why
The Go-first + Python-thin-client decision, the no-duplication rule, single-writer ownership of the event
store, and the five open forks (Go packaging, daemon vs library, who serves SSE, store-writer ownership,
Python-emit handoff) are not yet recorded; coding cannot start unrecorded (AGENTS.md reconciliation).

## Goal / value
An accepted ADR + design doc with RECONCILIATION + IMPACT REVIEW so the capability is governed before build.

## In scope
- ADR (docs/ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md) recording Go-core + Python-thin-client, no second bus/store.
- Design doc with the consumer migration matrix + no-regression DoD + the five open decisions.

## Out of scope
- Any implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
- ADR accepted; design doc lists frozen contracts, migration matrix, and resolved open decisions.
- language/ownership conflicts recorded (events.jsonl owner; event_bus facade).

## Verification / test plan
- `python scripts/dev/design_review_check.py docs/<design>.md` clean; ADR index updated.

decisions.decision: Go event core + Python thin client over the A1 seam; strangle consumers behind shims
Extend go/pfcore first (Q1); standalone Go bus daemon (Q2); SSE at API edge (Q3)
Python stays the event-store writer until a one-time Go cutover (Q4); emit via the seam (Q5)

prior_decisions: ADR-0001 / PF-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE-AND-IP-PLAN.md 4.8: Go-first for new work; no duplication
ENG-9-DOGFOOD.md:30: pipeline via the ONE canonical path (run_entry)
core/events.py:1-11: this module is the single writer of the canonical stream
BI-PF-0233: project-scoped bus events mirror into the per-project canonical stream
existing_path: orchestration signal bus + in-proc handlers -> core/event_bus.py
assumptions: A1 Go core is the acceptable host for the new bus
A2 core/events.py may become a thin client keeping its public API
A3 event-store writer ownership can cut over to Go with no second writer
A4 SSE served at the API edge (thin Python read), not a Go HTTP server
A5 subscriber-registry + alert-rule stores registered with single writers
A6 existing consumers accept in-proc shims with identical behavior
divergences: blocking/Go-daemon model diverges from the historical emit-and-read async design (DOGFOOD-E2E-DESIGN.md:65) -> amended by ADR-0005
legacy WebSocket transport is not extended (superseded by SSE)
open_questions: Q1 Go packaging: extend go/pfcore vs new go/eventbus -> extend go/pfcore first
Q2 run model: standalone Go bus daemon for dispatch/external delivery
Q4 writer ownership: Python now; Go one-time cutover later
Q5 Python-emit handoff: call the Go core (seam); no dual writer

impact_review.recommendation: do NOT; Python edge + Go behind seam
